standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the splitting pi used to build the endomorphisms p_i and the module structure that makes the obstruction computable.

standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the geometric condition 'direct sum of submodules' into algebraic equations whose entries generate J.

core_obligations: Choose a splitting pi : N_1 oplus N_2 -> M of s and let q_i be the projectors onto the summands, so that p_i = pi o q_i o s are endomorphisms of M with p_1 + p_2 = id_M (proof lines 28138-28140).
Establish the equivalence between 'M is a direct sum of submodules of N_1 oplus N_2' and 'p_1 and p_2 are orthogonal projectors' (proof lines 28141-28142).

Translate orthogonality of the projectors into the vanishing of p_1 o p_1 - p_1, p_2 o p_2 - p_2, p_1 o p_2 and p_2 o p_1, and define J as the smallest ideal of A whose extension to End_A(M) under J tensor_A End_A(M) contains all four (proof lines 28143-28145).
Conclude the stated factoring property for a ring map A -> B; the author states that some details are omitted (proof line 28146).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes finite projective A-modules M, N_1, N_2 and a split injection s : M -> N_1 oplus N_2, and asserts the existence of a finitely generated ideal J of A such that a ring map A -> B factors through A/J exactly when s tensor id_B identifies M tensor B with a direct sum of submodules of N_1 tensor B oplus N_2 tensor B (source lines 28126-28135). The proof chooses a splitting pi, defines the composite projectors p_i = pi o q_i o s with p_1 + p_2 = id_M, and observes that the desired direct-sum condition is equivalent to p_1 and p_2 being orthogonal projectors (proof lines 28138-28142). The real work is then encoding that equivalence as the vanishing of the four endomorphisms p_1 o p_1 - p_1, p_2 o p_2 - p_2, p_1 o p_2 and p_2 o p_1, which forces J to be the smallest ideal containing the entries of those endomorphisms under the identification J tensor End_A(M) (proof lines 28143-28145). The author leaves the remaining details omitted.
